newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X holders would get about half Placer.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X holders would get about half Placer.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday that shareholders of Bre-X Minerals Ltd would end up owning 45 to 55 percent of Placer if a merger of the two companies proceeded under Placer's proposal.

Placer said today it proposed a stock swap "merger of equals" that would be accounted as a pooling of interests. Placer chief executive John Willson told reporters that Canadian rules on pooling-of-interests required Bre-X holders to own 45 to 55 percent of the resulting company. Bre-X chief executive David Walsh would become Placer's biggest single shareholder, he said.
The US$1.7 billion cost of a mine at Bre-X's Busang gold discovery in Indonesia would be financed mainly by Placer's operating cash flow, chief financial officer Ian Austin said.
Cash flow was running at US$200 million to US$300 million a year and was due to rise to to US$400 million to US$500 million a year early in 1997, he said.
Willson said he would not be surprised if a bidding war developed for Bre-X.

He said Placer hopes for an open process to be organized for a deal with Bre-X. If this happens it could draw out rival bids, including from Barrick Gold Gorp which already has a joint venture proposal with Bre-X.
"We would not be surprised to find ourselves in a bidding war," Willson said, adding that he knew of at least four other mining compoanies likely to be interested.
Willson said the Placer proposal was worth about US$5 billion, or roughly the market capitalization of Placer. This does not include the value of the US$1.7 billion mine costs.
Placer said the companies combined would be worth about US$10 billion, so the offer to Bre-X holders would be about half that.
Although Barrick would likely seek to block Placer, Placer expected a positive response from Bre-X and the Indonesian government, Willson said.

He said the Indonesian government was sensitive "to the sense that what has been done may not be fair to Bre-X and the Bre-X shareholders." Moreover, he said there was a "lot of sentiment in Indonesia that a 10 percent ownership for the government seems rather low."
Under the Barrick deal, Indonesia would get a 10 percent stake.

Placer said its plan would entail a higher participation, but Willson could not specify how much it would be. Indonesian interests would receive 40 percent of the project in total, but that would include minority investors and the public.

Bre-X claims control over 90 percent of the rich Busang property and 10 percent is in the hands of its Indonesian partner. Bre-X has also promised a 10 percent slice to the son of Indonesian President Suharto conditional on the granting of contract-of-work permits.
Willson said he expected it to take weeks and perhaps months for the process to unwind. The Indonesian government appeared to be "in no great rush to reach a conclusion," he said.

Willson said Placer recently received "some encouragement" that its proposal would be well received, but he declined to be more specific. Willson said his company did not expect it would "be making agreements with any people within the Suharto family or within top government circles for services."

Placer would "reprioritize" its capital spending plans and some smaller projects might fall by the wayside if the Bre-X deal went ahead. But Willson said its Las Cristinas mine project in Venezuela would proceed.
